english: Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&5\end{pmatrix}$. For each positive integer $n$, let $s_n$ denote the sum of all the entries of $A^{n}$ and let $t_n$ denote the trace of $A^{n}$. Then the value of $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\dfrac{t_n}{s_n}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&5\end{pmatrix}$ है। प्रत्येक धनात्मक पूर्णांक $n$ के लिए माना $s_n$, $A^{n}$ की सभी प्रविष्टियों का योग है तथा $t_n$, $A^{n}$ का अनुरेख (trace) है। तब $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\dfrac{t_n}{s_n}$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: The $(1,2)$ entries $1,6,31$ are $1$, $1+5$, $1+5+25$, i.e. $\dfrac{5^{n}-1}{4}$. Claim: $A^{n}=\begin{pmatrix}1&\frac{5^{n}-1}{4}\\0&5^{n}\end{pmatrix}$ for all $n\ge1$.

The claim holds for $n=1$. If it holds for $n$, then $A^{n+1}=A^{n}A=\begin{pmatrix}1\cdot1&1\cdot1+\frac{5^{n}-1}{4}\cdot5\\0&5^{n}\cdot5\end{pmatrix}$, and $1+\dfrac{5^{n+1}-5}{4}=\dfrac{5^{n+1}-1}{4}$. So it holds for $n+1$, and by induction for all $n$.
originality_note: New: a ratio of two matrix invariants (trace and entry sum) of A^n is taken to the limit, so the closed form of A^n by induction is needed (way 5). Closest known: 'find A^n for an upper triangular 2 x 2 matrix by induction'. Different because: the question asks for the limit of t_n/s_n, which needs the exact growth of both quantities.
blueprint_concepts: Higher integral powers of a square matrices
Higher powers A^n by pattern recognition and induction

concept_use.Higher integral powers of a square matri: The trace and the entry sum of A^n are needed for every n, so A^n must be known in closed form.
concept_use.Higher powers A^n by pattern recognition: The pattern 1, 6, 31 for the (1,2) entry gives A^n = [[1, (5^n - 1)/4],[0, 5^n]], proved by induction.
